paper_id: Reliable Microservice Tail Latency Prediction via Decoupled Dual-Stream Learning and Gradient Modulation
title: Reliable Microservice Tail Latency Prediction via Decoupled Dual-Stream Learning and Gradient Modulation
motivation: Microservice tail latency prediction fails due to misaligned feature representations from mixing heterogeneous traffic and resource signals
problem_framing: Formulates latency prediction as snapshot spatial regression over aggregate dependency graph, explicitly separating demand from capacity
key_insight: Decouple physical modeling of traffic propagation (GNN) from resource saturation (gMLP) and modulate gradients to prevent one stream from dominating
method_signature: Dual-stream GNN+gMLP with hierarchical tensor fusion and reliability-aware gradient modulation (RAGM)
evaluation_criteria: MAPE, MAE, RMSE on window-level P95 latency across Online Boutique, Sock Shop, Train Ticket benchmarks
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Framework prioritizes instantaneous spatial states, inherently limiting exploitation of long-term temporal dependencies
evidence_for_taste: lack of explicit separation causes misaligned feature representations
unified architectures fail to isolate cascading dependencies
resource features converge faster and dominate gradient updates
the model overfits to the fast-converging infrastructure capacity signals
this entanglement fails to address structural dichotomy
